title: A Recovery-Adjusted Work Floor: A Lean Proof that Recovered Supply Lowers, and Exactly Attains, the Fresh-Supply Requirement
abstract: A recovery process supplies work to reach a useful-work target T from two sources: fresh supply wf and recovered supply wr, converted at modeled efficiencies ef and er that share a common cap emax > 0. We give a Lean 4 proof, against Mathlib, of the sealed statement P3.RecoveryWorkFloor. Part 1 (floor): if useful work ef*wf + er*wr reaches T, then the fresh supply is at least (T - emax*wr)/emax. Part 2 (attainment): whenever emax*wr <= T, the fresh supply (T - emax*wr)/emax is nonnegative and, run at the cap, delivers exactly T, so the floor cannot be raised. The proof derives the floor from a restatement of target_requires_supply of the Useful and Dissipated Work Ledger (Run-163): total supply must be at least T/emax, and the recovered part moves across the inequality. The floor is a bound on modeled efficiency only. It is not a Landauer bound, it does not use the Intelligence Bound conjecture, and it makes no claim about any real efficiency or recovered supply.

claims.text: For all reals wf, wr, ef, er, emax, T with wf, wr >= 0, 0 <= ef, er <= emax and emax > 0: if T <= ef*wf + er*wr then (T - emax*wr)/emax <= wf. For all wr >= 0, emax > 0 and T >= emax*wr: (T - emax*wr)/emax >= 0 and emax*((T - emax*wr)/emax) + emax*wr = T.

next_steps: P3.RecoveryWorkFloor has a candidate proof that passed viridis-lean-check (preview). The floor is derived from a restated Run-163 target_requires_supply. Next: prove P3.CyclicSymbiosis, the last P3 statement (sketch in 2026-11-05 notes: prev is a bijection on the cycle, Finset.prod_lt_prod_of_nonempty for one direction, explicit flow with lam = (prod v/c)^(1/N) for the other). Open question for Justin: is a per-source-cap variant (ef <= ef_max, er <= er_max) or a coupling of wr to the loop model (wr proportional to r*D) worth sealing?
